overview: Although titled as a fisheries file, these 258 pages chiefly document Allied plans for controlling Japan’s postwar production, especially its aluminum and magnesium industries. They include a guide to occupation administration, wartime laws and industry regulations, and technical and statistical appendices. Brief correspondence addresses Kurile fishing recruitment, Japanese seed oysters, and cultured pearls.
interest: The file’s fisheries title masks extensive evidence on wartime industrial administration and Allied plans to dismantle light metals production.
